chapters.title: Chapter 4: Income That Does Not Follow the Slabs

lessons.title: Special Rate Incomes: Capital Gains, Lottery Winnings and Crypto

body.text: Not every rupee climbs the slab staircase. Some income is pulled out and taxed at its own fixed rate, whatever your salary. For equity gains that rate can be far below your slab rate; for lottery winnings and crypto it can be far above it.

markDefs.definition: Income that the law taxes at a fixed rate specified for that type of income, instead of at the slab rates. It is still part of Total Income.

children.text: A college student in Kochi with no other income who wins ₹10 lakh on the Kerala State Lottery pays over ₹3 lakh in tax. A retired engineer in Pune who books ₹10 lakh of long-term gains on his Nifty index fund pays about ₹1.1 lakh. Neither number comes from the slab table. Both are examples of
, and knowing which incomes fall into this bucket is essential before you trust any slab calculation.
The Main Special Rates for Individuals

body.caption: Special-Rate Income, Tax Year 2026-27 (Before Surcharge and Cess)

cells: Short-term gains on listed equity shares, equity mutual funds and business trust units
Held 12 months or less, STT paid
Long-term gains on the same assets
Held more than 12 months, STT paid
Long-term gains on other assets, such as property, gold, unlisted shares and listed bonds
Held more than 24 months (12 months for listed securities)
Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, card games, horse races, betting and gambling
Income from transfer of virtual digital assets, such as crypto and NFTs
Only cost of acquisition deductible; losses cannot be set off

body.text: Not all capital gains get a special rate. Short-term gains on property, gold, unlisted shares and debt funds are added to your slab income and taxed at slab rates. So are all gains on debt mutual fund units bought on or after 1 April 2023, however long you hold them. Only the categories in the table above leave the slab system.

columns.label: Slab-Rate Income
points: Salary, rent, business profits, interest, most dividends
Taxed at rising rates from nil to 30%
Benefits from the nil slab and the lower slabs
Eligible for the new regime rebate up to ₹12 lakh

columns.label: Special-Rate Income
points: Equity capital gains, long-term gains on other assets, lottery, online games, crypto
Taxed at one fixed rate: 12.5%, 20% or 30%
Can use unused nil slab only in limited cases (see below)
Not eligible for the new regime rebate

children.text: Equity Gains: Usually Cheaper Than Your Slab

Sana, a product designer in Bengaluru with ₹30 lakh of salary income, sells two holdings through Zerodha in tax year 2026-27. She has ₹3,00,000 of gains on a Nifty 50 index fund held for four years, and ₹50,000 of gains on shares of Tata Power held for seven months.

Had those ₹3,50,000 of gains been taxed at Sana's 30% slab, the tax with cess would have been ₹1,09,200. Special rates save her ₹76,050. For most salaried investors above the 20% slab, equity gains are the most lightly taxed income they have.
Lottery and Gaming Winnings: 30% From the First Rupee

Winnings from lotteries, game shows, betting and gambling are taxed at a flat 30% with no nil slab, no rebate and no deductions. It does not matter that the winner has no other income. Online gaming winnings, including fantasy sports platforms, follow a similar 30% rule on net winnings.

stats.label: Joseph's Lottery Prize
stats.context: Kerala State Lottery, no other income

body.text: Tax on winnings is usually collected before the prize reaches you. The payer deducts TDS at 30% on lottery and similar winnings above ₹10,000 from a single payout, and on net online gaming winnings. Always check Form 26AS and AIS to confirm the deduction appears against your PAN.

children.text: Crypto and Other Virtual Digital Assets: 30% and No Loss Relief

Gains on crypto, NFTs and other virtual digital assets are taxed at 30%. Only the cost of acquisition can be deducted, not exchange fees or internet costs. And a loss on one virtual digital asset cannot be set off against a gain on another, against any other income, or carried forward to a later year. Each profitable trade is taxed in isolation.

body.caption: Rohit's Crypto Trades on an Indian Exchange, Tax Year 2026-27

cells: Ignored. Cannot reduce the Bitcoin gain or be carried forward

body.text: Rohit's actual economic profit is ₹1,20,000, but he pays ₹62,400 of tax on it, an effective rate of 52%. A 1% TDS is also deducted on the sale value of crypto transfers above specified limits, which ties up cash even on loss-making trades until it is adjusted in the return.

children.text: Using the Unused Nil Slab Against Capital Gains

There is one important bridge between the two systems. If a resident individual's slab-rate income is below the nil slab, the unused part of the nil slab can be used to reduce short-term gains on listed equity, long-term gains on listed equity, and long-term gains on other assets. It cannot be used against lottery winnings, online gaming winnings or crypto gains, and non-residents cannot use it at all.

body.label: Unused Nil Slab Adjustment
body.value: Nil slab minus slab-rate income, if positive
body.context: New regime: ₹4,00,000 minus slab-rate income. Available to resident individuals and HUFs against listed equity gains and long-term capital gains, but not against lottery, gaming or crypto income.

body.title: Going deeper: the 60% rate on unexplained income

children.text: The harshest special rate applies to unexplained cash credits, investments, money or expenditure that a taxpayer cannot satisfactorily explain during an assessment. Such income is taxed at 60%, with a 25% surcharge and 4% cess on top, taking the effective rate to 78%. No deductions or set-offs are allowed against it. It exists to discourage undisclosed income and is almost never relevant to salaried taxpayers who report their income correctly.

body.title: Tax on Harish's Equity Gains
body.prompt: Harish, a chartered accountant in Surat with ₹22 lakh of salary income, sells listed shares through Groww in tax year 2026-27. He has ₹4,00,000 of long-term gains on shares held for three years and ₹1,00,000 of short-term gains on shares held for six months. What is his tax on these gains, before cess?
body.explanation: Short-term gains: 20% of ₹1,00,000 = ₹20,000. Long-term gains: 12.5% of (₹4,00,000 − ₹1,25,000) = 12.5% of ₹2,75,000 = ₹34,375. Total: ₹54,375 before cess. His salary is well above the nil slab, so there is no unused nil slab to adjust.

body.title: Crypto Losses
body.question: Ritu, a resident in Hyderabad, makes a gain of ₹3,00,000 selling Solana and a loss of ₹1,00,000 selling Dogecoin in tax year 2026-27. She also has a ₹50,000 short-term loss on listed shares. What is her tax on crypto, before cess?
options: ₹45,000, taxing the ₹1,50,000 net result of all three at 30%
₹60,000, taxing the ₹2,00,000 net crypto gain at 30%
₹90,000, taxing the full ₹3,00,000 Solana gain at 30%
body.explanation: A loss on one virtual digital asset cannot be set off against a gain on another, and a share loss cannot be set off against crypto gains either. The full ₹3,00,000 Solana gain is taxed at 30%: ₹90,000 before cess. The share loss follows normal capital loss rules and can be set off against other capital gains or carried forward.

body.title: Lottery Rate
body.textWithBlank: Lottery winnings are taxed at a flat rate of ___%, with no nil slab and no deductions.
body.explanation: The 30% rate applies from the very first rupee of winnings, plus surcharge where applicable and 4% cess. Even a winner with no other income cannot use the nil slab or the rebate against it.

body.title: Lata's Index Fund Gains
body.scenario: Lata, 58, is a resident homemaker in Nashik. In tax year 2026-27 her only income is ₹1,50,000 of FD interest and ₹5,00,000 of long-term gains from redeeming a Nifty 50 index fund she held for eight years. She is on the new regime. Her son says: "Your total income is only ₹6.5 lakh, so the rebate means you pay nothing."
body.prompt: Is her son right? Work out Lata's tax, using the unused nil slab where allowed.
body.modelAnswer: Her son is wrong. Lata's slab-rate income is ₹1,50,000, well below the ₹4,00,000 nil slab, so ₹2,50,000 of the nil slab is unused. As a resident, she can use it to reduce her long-term equity gains to ₹5,00,000 − ₹2,50,000 = ₹2,50,000. The first ₹1,25,000 of long-term equity gains is exempt, leaving ₹1,25,000 taxed at 12.5%: ₹15,625. Under the new regime, the rebate cannot be used against tax on special-rate income, even though her Total Income of ₹6,50,000 is below ₹12 lakh. With 4% cess she pays ₹16,250. Her FD interest is fully covered by the nil slab, so it carries no tax.

cards.definition: 20%, for shares, equity mutual funds and business trust units held 12 months or less with STT paid.
12.5% on gains above ₹1,25,000 a year, for holdings over 12 months with STT paid.
12.5% without indexation, for property, gold and unlisted shares held over 24 months.
30% flat from the first rupee, with no deductions, nil slab or rebate.
30% on gains; only cost of acquisition deductible; losses cannot be set off or carried forward.
60% plus 25% surcharge plus 4% cess, an effective 78%.

points: Special-rate income is part of Total Income but is taxed at its own fixed rate, not through the slabs
Listed equity gains are taxed at 20% (short term) and 12.5% above ₹1,25,000 (long term), usually below a salaried investor's slab rate
Lottery, betting, online gaming winnings and crypto gains are taxed at 30% from the first rupee
Crypto losses cannot be set off against any income or carried forward
Short-term gains on property, gold, unlisted shares and newer debt funds are taxed at slab rates, not special rates
Resident individuals can use an unused nil slab against equity and long-term capital gains, but not against lottery or crypto income
Under the new regime, the rebate cannot be used against tax on special-rate income

body.text: Rates shown apply to resident individuals for tax year 2026-27, based on the rates in force since 23 July 2024. Section references are to the Income-tax Act, 1961 for familiarity; the Income-tax Act, 2025 carries equivalent provisions under new section numbers. Capital gains rules have many conditions not covered here. This lesson is for education only and is not tax or investment advice.
